defect_observations.note: A witness for the C003 flat-prior claim exists in thm:p15-bayes-transformation (uniform in theta vs uniform in eta=theta^2; proof handbook/annex/p15/bayesian-updating-prediction.tex lines 371-392), but C003 does not cross-reference it and it addresses posterior means, not the marginal likelihood m_k (e.g. one Bernoulli success gives m=1/2 under uniform theta and m=2/3 under uniform eta; not stated anywhere).
C003 states the intrinsic weight identity only 'on the appropriate almost-everywhere domains'; the domain {sum_l alpha_l r_l > 0} is named only in the proof (annex lines 83-85).

Notation variant not recorded: the handbook's alpha_k are prior probabilities summing to one, while the held source's eq (16) (p. 784, PDF p. 13) uses alpha_k = pr(H_k)/pr(H_0), prior odds against H_0 with B_00 = alpha_0 = 1. The reference-model form of (16) is not shown and the symbol clash is not flagged, although the B_ij index convention is flagged 'as in the source'. The two weight formulas are equivalent, so this is not scored as a coverage failure.

The held source (p. 781, Sec 5.1) faults the conditional prescription pi(beta|psi=psi_0,H_1) for parameterization dependence (change of variables with Jacobian; Savage/Borel paradox). The handbook (body lines 197-202, 391-396 and 408-414) instead uses an almost-everywhere modification of the conditional kernel at the single point psi=1/2. That mechanism is weaker than the source's, because continuous canonical versions still conflict across parameterizations. The handbook does not misattribute; it only leaves the source's mechanism unreproduced.
The second paragraph of C006 does not restate the null-centered hypothesis, which it inherits from line 247. The proof (annex lines 242-253) uses the centered formula.
The C002 proof compresses the tagged posterior step ('Multiplication by w_k gives the tagged posterior formula') without displaying alpha_k int_A f_k dPi_k / e(x). It is accepted as a written step.

C004's final sentence ('No equality of nuisance priors in different models is automatic') has no step in its declared proof (annex lines 123-158). It is supported only by the body's forward pointer (lines 201-202) to the C011 null-constraint example.
